title: Effect of intercritical annealing on microstructure, texture, tensile properties, and fracture of laser welded medium Manganese steel
abstract: In this study, the effects of intercritical annealing heat treatment (IAHT, 650 °C for 5min) on the microstructure, texture, tensile properties, and fracture of the laser welded MMS joints were systematically investigated. The as-welded joint shows poor strength and ductility, with brittle fracture occurring in the FZ. After IAHT, the area fraction of reverted austenite (γrev) increased heterogeneously across the joint: 29.6 % in the inter-critical HAZ, 16.4 % in the FZ, and 8.9 % in the coarse-grained HAZ; concurrently, the overall hardness of the joint is significantly reduced. The increased γrev further activates the transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effect and enhances work hardening. EBSD-EDS analysis demonstrated that IAHT promoted Mn partitioning, greatly reduced the average KAM and GND density of the FZ, and homogenized the grain structure. Following IAHT, the Goss texture in the BCC phase was strengthened owing to its low interfacial energy and thus high thermodynamic stability. Additionally, the Kurdjumov-Sachs (K–S) orientation relationships became more prominent in the FZ as γrev nucleates in accordance with the K–S orientation relationship. As a result, the mechanical properties of the joint are significantly enhanced, with the fracture mode shifted from brittle fracture in the FZ to ductile fracture in the HAZ.
